pages.title: Cantor Diagonalizer
pages.text: Cantor's trick, built in brass: list every number, then build one that differs from the n-th at its n-th digit - a number on no list. It manufactures infinities, then bigger ones.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 6$() machine.
$(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry - and JEI - show the pattern.

It takes the computational power of a superintelligence and points it at infinity.$(br2)Odd result today: $(item)Banach-Tarski Spheres$() can be split and reassembled into two. In real maths that is a theorem, not a trick - the pieces are so strange that 'volume' stops applying to them.

$(thing)Machine data$(): a single-block machine (6 item and 2 fluid inputs, 2 and 0 outputs).$(br2)$(thing)Makes$(): Absolute Infinity, Aleph-Null Shard, Banach-Tarski Sphere, Continuum Shard, Godel Sentence, Hilbert's Hotel Key, Hypersphere Fragment, Inaccessible Cardinal, Ordinal Stone, Russell Paradox Set, Surreal Number.
Cut it into five non-measurable pieces, reassemble them, and you have two spheres.$(br2)Made in $(item)Cantor Diagonalizer$().
$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Banach-Tarski Sphere$(): Absolute Notes I, Axiomatic Breach Engine, Banach-Tarski Sphere, Transfinite Casing
